Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct (36 layers, 32 heads with GQA 4:1, MLP width 12288). 7 parts passed the screen. All are large units chosen from the weights first.

ARITHMETIC (two_digit_addition, my own skill; control = copy the first operand):
1. L23 attention heads [4,7,30,31]: addition drop .414, control -.002, random parts at most .125. Picked by OV digit-copy score: digit embedding mapped to the same digit's unembedding, 5.7/5.2/4.7 for heads 30/7/4 against under 1 for word, CJK, accented, code and Cyrillic tokens.
2. The same group grown to 8 heads [4,7,20,25,28,29,30,31]: drop .463. Two of the five random parts reached .26 and .22, so the margin is smaller.
3. L23 MLP, 256 units: drop .433, random parts at most .009.
4. L23 MLP, 512 units: drop .438, random parts at most .003. Both clusters were built from weights alone: an SVD of the L23 digit-head OV outputs on digit tokens gives a 12-dim subspace, and I took the MLP units whose gate and up rows read most from it.
- The head group also generalises. The 4 heads cut subtraction .314, and the 8 heads cut month_successor .266. The subtraction screen failed only because addition is the other skill that drops. The month result was not screened, because its control moved -.147, past the ±.089 limit.
- Readers of the L23 subspace at L24 cut both addition .349 and subtraction .215. Readers of other layers' own digit heads (L22/24/26/29) did nothing.

NUMBER EMISSION (recall_first_number: recall the first element of a Python list after a comment; control = the same with a list of words):
5–7. L34 MLP number-writer clusters of 64, 128 and 256 units. Drops were .533 / .544 / .603 with word control near 0 and random parts at most .003. Picked purely by the cosine between each down_proj column and the digit unembedding direction. The logit lens of the top units is exactly the digits 0–9, or a bare space token traded against digits.

FACTS (built-in):
8. Whole block L30: facts drop .353, every other skill at most .111. It passed, but random single blocks reached .298, so the margin is thin. Almost all of the effect sits in the L30 MLP (.29) rather than its attention (.027), and it is spread out: 2048-unit subsets ranked by weights gave only .06. The 2-layer block L29–30 dropped facts .635 but failed, because a random 2-layer block reached .727.

NEGATIVE RESULTS:
- Writer clusters for month, colour, capital, CJK, accented and code tokens at L24–35 were not bottlenecks (drops at most .01). Their skills have margins of about 11 nats. The digit writers were the exception, at a margin of about 3.4 nats.
- Heads picked by OV maps for English→French and country→capital only tracked their copy scores and had no causal effect.
- Attribution scans keep at most 20 units per layer and missed the L23 heads entirely. The weight-first approach did better on this model.
- Multilingual hits (about .1) from L34 clusters came from overlap with the digit writers.
